subject: business-studies
title: Marketing Mix Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll dive deep into the 4 Ps — what each one means and why they must work together.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies marketing mix foundations — Product, Price, Place, Promotion deep-dive.
final_note: You can describe each of the 4 Ps and explain why they must be consistent.

concepts.def: What the firm sells — features, quality, design
What customers pay — must reflect value
Where and how the product reaches customers
How customers find out about the product
Wrapping that protects and promotes a product
Path goods take from producer to customer

walkthroughs.body_html:
The product is the core of the mix.

Includes design, features, quality, brand, packaging. A weak product can't be saved by clever advertising.

Place = distribution channels.

Direct (producer → customer, e.g. website) or indirect (via wholesalers/retailers). Wider reach = more sales but lower margin per unit.

A luxury watch sold in £1 shops with crude packaging would contradict the brand.

The 4 Ps must be consistent with each other and with the target market.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Corporate governance is the legal requirement to have a CEO.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
A brand is just the logo on a product.

mcqs.q: What is corporate governance, and how does it differ from CSR?
options: Corporate governance is the legal requirement to have a CEO.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

Corporate governance is the system of rules, practices and processes by which a company is directed and controlled — focusing on accountability, board structure and shareholder rights. CSR is about wider social/environmental responsibility.
Corporate governance is the same as corporate social responsibility.
